answer: Brie goes best with fig jam, pears, honey and walnuts, on a plain baguette or water cracker. Sweet, juicy and crunchy partners give a mild, creamy cheese the contrast it's missing.

faq.a: Pears, apples, grapes, figs and apricots. Juicy fruit cuts the butterfat.
Champagne or sparkling wine first, then oaked Chardonnay or a light red like Pinot Noir or Beaujolais.

answer: Camembert goes best with baguette, apples, dry cider and other bloomy-rind cheeses. It's stronger and more mushroomy than brie, so pair it with crisp, fresh partners.

faq.a: Camembert is smaller, stronger and earthier. Choose it if brie tastes bland to you.
Dry Normandy cider is the classic; Chardonnay and Beaujolais work too.

answer: Aged cheddar goes best with crisp apples, chutney, whole-grain mustard, pickles and honey. Sharp, salty cheddar needs sweet or tart partners to balance it.

faq.q: What fruit goes with sharp cheddar?
faq.a: Apples above all, plus pears, grapes and dried cranberries.

faq.q: What drink goes with aged cheddar?
faq.a: Cabernet Sauvignon, dry cider, IPA or stout. Cheddar is one of the most drink-friendly cheeses.

answer: Aged Gouda goes best with dark chocolate, apples, smoked almonds and dried fruit. Its caramel, butterscotch flavor and crunchy crystals suit sweet and toasty partners.

faq.a: Those crystals are amino acids that form as the cheese ages. They mean flavor, not a flaw.

faq.q: What wine goes with aged Gouda?
faq.a: Cabernet, Merlot or tawny port. Its caramel notes also love stout and Belgian dubbel.

answer: Manchego goes best with membrillo (quince paste), chorizo, Marcona almonds, olives and jamón. Spain's nutty sheep's cheese loves the salty, sweet and smoky foods it grew up beside.

faq.a: A firm, sweet quince paste from Spain, sliced thin and laid on Manchego.
Spanish reds like Rioja or Tempranillo, dry rosé, or fino sherry.

answer: Gruyère goes best with cornichons, Dijon mustard, ham, hazelnuts and roasted chestnuts. Nutty, sweet-savory Alpine cheese needs sour, sharp or toasty partners.

faq.a: Cooked ham, speck and dried beef like Bündnerfleisch.
Pinot Noir, Chardonnay or a dry Alpine white. Lager and dry cider work too.

answer: Comté goes best with walnuts, pears, hazelnuts, saucisson sec and baguette. Its brown-butter, nutty flavor pairs with more nuts and fresh fruit.

faq.a: Very similar mountain cheeses. Comté is a little sweeter and fruitier; Gruyère is a little saltier.
Chardonnay, Champagne, Pinot Noir or Beaujolais.

answer: Parmigiano-Reggiano goes best with balsamic glaze, pears, dried figs, prosciutto and honey. Salty, savory crystals love sweet and tart partners from the same Italian region.

faq.q: How do you serve Parmigiano on a board?
faq.a: Break it into rough chunks with a short knife rather than slicing. The crystals show better.
Chianti, Lambrusco or Champagne.

answer: Pecorino Romano goes best with honey, black pepper, cherry preserves, olives and cured pork. It's very salty and sharp, so small pieces with sweet partners work best.

faq.q: Is Pecorino Romano too salty for a board?
faq.a: Not in small pieces. Serve it with honey or fruit preserves to balance the salt.
Chianti, Sangiovese or a light Italian white.

answer: Gorgonzola goes best with pears, honey, walnuts, figs and dark chocolate. Sweet, juicy and crunchy partners tame blue cheese's salt and sharpness.

faq.a: Dolce is soft and mild, easier for guests; piccante is firmer and sharper.
Port or a sweet dessert wine. Among dry wines, try an Italian red with some fruit.

answer: Stilton goes best with walnuts, honey, oatcakes, dried fruit and port. Its crumbly, salty richness needs sweetness and crunch.

faq.a: Port is the classic. Stout and sweet dessert wine work too.
Medium. It's creamier and milder than Roquefort, stronger than Cambozola.

answer: Fresh goat cheese goes best with honey, figs, pistachios, fresh berries and herbs. Sweet and crunchy partners soften its bright tang.

faq.q: What wine goes with goat cheese?
faq.a: Sauvignon Blanc, especially from the Loire. Dry rosé and sparkling wine work too.

faq.q: How do you serve chèvre on a board?
faq.a: Roll a log in herbs, nuts or pepper, or drizzle it with honey.

answer: Burrata goes best with prosciutto, basil, good olive oil, ripe tomatoes, peaches and flaky salt. Its cool, milky center needs salt, acid and a little crunch.

faq.q: How long can burrata sit out?
faq.a: Serve it cold and set out no more than about an hour before eating; it's a fresh cheese.
Dry rosé, Sauvignon Blanc or Prosecco.

answer: Taleggio goes best with prosciutto, speck, crusty bread, pears and Riesling or Belgian ale. Its funky rind and mild, buttery center suit cured ham and fruity drinks.

faq.a: The rind does; the inside is mild and buttery. Let it breathe on the board.
Off-dry Riesling, Belgian ale or Pinot Noir.

answer: Fresh mozzarella goes best with basil, olive oil, tomatoes, prosciutto and balsamic glaze. It's mild and milky, so bright, salty and herbal partners do the talking.

faq.a: Burrata is mozzarella with a creamy center. Use mozzarella for skewers, burrata for a centerpiece.
Light, crisp whites and dry rosé.

answer: Prosciutto goes best with melon, figs, fig jam, burrata, Parmigiano and pears. Sweet fruit and creamy cheese balance its silky saltiness.

faq.q: How do you arrange prosciutto on a board?
faq.a: Loose folds or ribbons, never flat sheets. Separate the slices so guests can pick one up.
Prosecco, dry rosé, Pinot Noir or Chianti.

answer: Genoa salami goes best with provolone, pickles, olives, mustard and crackers. Mild, garlicky salami is a team player that works with nearly every cheese.

faq.q: What cheese goes with Genoa salami?
faq.a: Provolone, mild cheddar, Gouda and triple-crème.

faq.q: How do you fold salami for a board?
faq.a: Fold rounds in half, then in half again, and line them up in a 'river'.

answer: Soppressata goes best with fresh mozzarella, hot honey, giardiniera, provolone and olives. Its coarse, peppery fat loves cool cheese and tangy pickles.

faq.a: Calabrese soppressata is; Veneto-style is mild. Check the label.
Chianti, Malbec or Cabernet.

answer: Spanish chorizo goes best with Manchego, membrillo, Marcona almonds, olives and roasted peppers. Smoky paprika pork belongs with Spanish cheese and salty snacks.

faq.q: Spanish or Mexican chorizo for a board?
faq.a: Spanish: it's cured and sliceable. Mexican chorizo is raw and must be cooked.
Rioja, Malbec or dry rosé.

answer: Mortadella goes best with pistachios, burrata, focaccia, giardiniera and Grana Padano. Silky, mild pork needs crunch, creaminess and a tangy pickle.

faq.q: How do you serve mortadella on a board?
faq.a: Thin slices, folded, or thick cubes on picks with pistachios.
Lambrusco, Prosecco or Chianti.

answer: Smoked salmon goes best with cream cheese, capers, pickled red onions, dill and rye or blini. Creamy and briny partners balance its rich smoke.

faq.q: Is smoked salmon safe on a board?
faq.a: Keep it cold and set it out last. Serve within about two hours.

faq.q: What wine goes with smoked salmon?
faq.a: Champagne, Sauvignon Blanc or unoaked Chardonnay.

answer: Fig jam goes best with brie, Manchego, blue cheese, prosciutto and walnuts. Its dense sweetness balances salty cheese and cured ham.

faq.q: What cheese goes with fig jam?
faq.a: Brie, Manchego, goat cheese and blue cheese.

faq.q: How much fig jam for a board?
faq.a: One small bowl, about 1/4 cup per 6 guests.

answer: Honey goes best with blue cheese, goat cheese, Pecorino, aged cheddar and walnuts. Sweetness softens salty and tangy cheeses.

faq.a: Salty or sharp ones: blue cheese, Pecorino and fresh goat cheese.
Honeycomb looks better and doesn't run; a honey dipper works in a small jar.

answer: Apples go best with aged cheddar, aged Gouda, Gruyère, pecans and walnuts. Crisp, tart apple cuts fat and resets your palate between bites.

faq.q: How do you stop apples browning on a board?
faq.a: Toss slices in a little lemon juice or cut them last.

faq.q: Which apple is best for cheese?
faq.a: Crisp, tart apples like Honeycrisp, Pink Lady or Granny Smith.

answer: Dark chocolate goes best with aged Gouda, blue cheese, hazelnuts, dried cherries and sea salt. Bitter cacao loves caramel, salt and toasted nuts.

faq.q: What cheese goes with dark chocolate?
faq.a: Aged Gouda first, then blue cheese and aged cheddar.

faq.q: What drink goes with dark chocolate?
faq.a: Port, Cabernet, Malbec or stout.
